instruction: Reviewer must create stable gold experiment IDs GOLD-Pxx-Eyyy from source evidence; A/G IDs are references only.

a_interpretation.title: Adaptive laboratory evolution of E. coli W under glycerol limitation
a_interpretation.intervention: serial batch cultivation in 50 mL M9 glycerol (0.2% v/v) medium, 250 mL flask, 37 degC with agitation, transfer every 12 h, initial OD600 stepwise 0.0008 -> 0.0004 -> 0.00016, ~1300 generations (Eq. 1)
a_interpretation.replicates: unknown (Fig. 1 caption missing; number of parallel lineages not stated in available text)
a_interpretation.readouts: estimated doubling time over generations (Fig. 1B), specific growth rate (Fig. 1C), glycerol consumption rate (Fig. 1D)
a_interpretation.outcomes: single clone CY02 isolated; growth rate 0.67 +/- 0.03 -> 0.94 +/- 0.01 /hr (~40% increase); increased glycerol consumption rate; negligible fitness change on glucose
a_interpretation.notes: Results text for this experiment is embedded in paragraph 1_introduction_p003 due to a parser section-misattribution; Fig. 1 caption absent.

a_interpretation.title: Whole-genome resequencing and causal-mutation nomination
a_interpretation.intervention: none (measurement)
a_interpretation.readouts: mutation calls vs NC_017635.1 after parental background subtraction
a_interpretation.analysis: shared-mutation focus between population and CY02 (Table 1, Fig. S1)
a_interpretation.outcomes: 93 (population) / 89 (CY02) total mutations; 30 / 28 new; shared notable: glpK T235M, crp R209H, ptsP Pro174fs, rsfS Gln6*, mglC Asn4fs

a_interpretation.title: Reverse engineering of glpK^m/crp^m and fitness/GUR characterization
a_interpretation.intervention: lambda-Red recombinase-mediated introduction of glpK T235M and crp R209H singly and in combination into parental W
a_interpretation.conditions: M9 minimal glycerol medium; exponential growth
a_interpretation.readouts: specific growth rate (Fig. 2A), specific glycerol uptake rate (Fig. 2B, Cedex)
a_interpretation.outcomes: growth: glpK^m 1.45-fold (p<0.022), double 1.56-fold (p=0.037), CY02 1.63-fold (p=0.009), crp^m n.s.; GUR: 1.78/1.70/1.60-fold for glpK^m strains, crp^m n.s.

a_interpretation.title: GlpK^w vs GlpK T235M expression, purification and enzyme kinetics
a_interpretation.intervention: cloning of WT/mutant glpK into pET28a(+) (N-terminal 6xHis), overexpression in BL21(DE3), Ni-NTA purification
a_interpretation.conditions: assay at 25 degC, pH 7.0, 200 uL reaction, 0.5 ug/mL enzyme; FBP 0-10 mM for allostery
a_interpretation.replicates: six replicates (WT enzyme), five replicates (mutant enzyme) per Fig. 2D caption; replicate type unspecified
a_interpretation.readouts: V0/Vmax, specific activity vs FBP; Vmax, Km_gly, kcat, kcat/Km, FBP K0.5 (Table 2)
a_interpretation.analysis: SigmaPlot 12 curve fitting; Eq. (4) allosteric fit
a_interpretation.outcomes: catalytic activity unchanged; mutant insensitive to FBP (K0.5 >10,000 uM vs 0.386 mM WT per text)

a_interpretation.title: Intracellular cAMP measurement
a_interpretation.intervention: none (measurement on engineered strains)
a_interpretation.conditions: exponential phase harvest; ice-cold 65% ethanol extraction
a_interpretation.analysis: one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc
a_interpretation.outcomes: glpK^m-harboring strains ~2% of WT; CY02 ~20% of WT; crp^m 36% of WT; all P<0.001

a_interpretation.title: RT-qPCR of glpK expression
a_interpretation.conditions: M9 glycerol, log phase
a_interpretation.controls: wild-type; normalization to rrsA or ihfB
a_interpretation.readouts: relative glpK mRNA abundance (Fig. S4, unavailable)
a_interpretation.analysis: StepOne Software v2.3; standard-curve primer efficiency
a_interpretation.outcomes: glpK^m-harboring strains 3-6% of WT; crp^m ~22%; double mutant < half of glpK^m

a_interpretation.title: RNA-seq transcriptome comparison WT vs CY02
a_interpretation.conditions: M9 minimal + 2 g/L glycerol; harvest OD600 0.4-0.5
a_interpretation.readouts: gene expression; DEGs; CRP regulon enrichment
a_interpretation.analysis: CLC Genomics Workbench trimming/mapping; DESeq2 (FC>2, adj P<0.01)
a_interpretation.outcomes: 640 DEGs (149 up / 491 down); 181 CRP-regulated DEGs; 148/157 positively regulated CRP genes downregulated; lower glycolysis up, TCA/respiration down, pta/ackA up, acs down

a_interpretation.title: Acetate secretion rate measurement
a_interpretation.conditions: exponential growth in M9 glycerol
a_interpretation.analysis: one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc
a_interpretation.outcomes: WT below accurate determination; CY02 and glpK^m-harboring mutants elevated; crp^m not determinable

a_interpretation.title: GABA production in M9 glycerol minimal medium
a_interpretation.conditions: 50 mL M9 glycerol (0.2% v/v) + 50 mg/L yeast extract, 250 mL flasks, biological triplicates
a_interpretation.outcomes: 0.06 +/- 0.01 g/L for both WT and CY02 (negligible difference)

a_interpretation.title: Medium and glycerol-concentration optimization for GABA production
a_interpretation.intervention: switch to amino acid-rich LB + glycerol; glycerol concentration screen using growth rate as proxy (Fig. S7, plate reader)
a_interpretation.conditions: LB + 2% (v/v) glycerol selected; stationary-phase GABA measurement
a_interpretation.readouts: specific growth rate (proxy screen); final GABA concentration
a_interpretation.outcomes: highest growth at 2% glycerol; stationary GABA: WT 0.05, crp^m 0.06, glpK^m 0.07, double 0.07, CY02 0.17 g/L
a_interpretation.notes: Fig. S7 data unavailable; proxy assumption (growth-coupled GABA production) is an author assumption, not validated causality.

a_interpretation.title: Time-course GABA production WT vs CY02 in LB + 2% glycerol
a_interpretation.conditions: 50 mL LB + 2% (v/v) glycerol, 250 mL flasks, 37 degC, 200 rpm, over 24 h, biological triplicates
a_interpretation.readouts: growth, glycerol consumption (HPLC-RID), GABA (dansyl chloride HPLC-UV 286 nm)
a_interpretation.outcomes: WT max 0.15 +/- 0.01 g/L, 0.03 +/- 0.01 g/L/hr; CY02 0.39 +/- 0.03 g/L, 0.08 +/- 0.01 g/L/hr (~2.6-fold); glycerol consumption similar

a_interpretation.title: Targeted knockout of metabolic sinks (ackA, mgsA, gabT) in CY02 and WT backgrounds
a_interpretation.intervention: lambda-Red KanR replacement and pCP20 marker excision to delete ackA, mgsA, gabT singly, in double combinations, and as triple knockout
a_interpretation.conditions: LB + 2% (v/v) glycerol, flask batch, biological triplicates
a_interpretation.readouts: growth, glycerol consumption, GABA titer/productivity (Fig. 6, Fig. S8, Table 3)
a_interpretation.outcomes: single KOs lower than comparator; doubles 0.46/0.45/0.37 g/L; CY02_TKO 0.59 +/- 0.04 g/L and 0.13 +/- 0.02 g/L/hr (1.5-/1.6-fold over CY02; 3.9-/4.3-fold over WT); benefit of double/triple KOs absent in WT background; ΔackA strains prolonged lag phase

g_interpretation.intervention: serial batch ALE under glycerol limitation
g_interpretation.conditions: M9 + 0.2% (v/v) glycerol, 50 mL/250 mL flask, 37 °C, agitation, transfer every 12 h, initial OD600 0.0008 -> 0.0004 -> 0.00016 (implemented design values)

g_interpretation.readout: MiSeq 50-cycle SE; mutations vs NC_017635.1 after parental background subtraction
g_interpretation.outcome: 93 (population) / 89 (CY02) total; 30 / 28 new; shared mutations in rsfS, mglC, ptsP, crp, glpK (Table 1)

g_interpretation.intervention: lambda-Red reverse engineering of point mutations (validation of causality, not a production design decision)
g_interpretation.readout: specific growth rate, glycerol uptake rate (Cedex), biological duplicates
g_interpretation.outcome: glpK^m 1.45-fold growth / 1.78-fold GUR; crp^m not significant; CY02 1.63-fold / 1.60-fold

g_interpretation.intervention: heterologous overexpression and Ni-NTA purification of GlpK^w and GlpK^m
g_interpretation.readout: coupled enzyme assay, A340, 25 °C pH 7.0; FBP 0-10 mM; n=6 (WT) / n=5 (CY02) for SA
g_interpretation.outcome: catalytic activity unchanged; FBP inhibition lost in T235M (K0.5 > 10,000 μM vs 386 μM)

g_interpretation.readout: intracellular cAMP ELISA, exponential phase; biological triplicates x technical duplicates; one-way ANOVA + Tukey
g_interpretation.outcome: cAMP ~2% of WT in glpK^m strains; CY02 ~20%; crp^m 36%

g_interpretation.readout: RNA-seq (HiSeq 50-cycle SE), M9 + 2 g/L glycerol, OD600 0.4-0.5, biological triplicates, DESeq2 (FC>2, adjP<0.01)
g_interpretation.outcome: 640 DEGs (149 up / 491 down); 181 CRP regulons; 148/157 positively regulated CRP genes downregulated

g_interpretation.readout: RT-qPCR glpK, rrsA/ihfB normalization, 2 biological x 3 technical
g_interpretation.outcome: glpK expression 3-6% of WT in glpK^m backgrounds; ~22% in crp^m; double mutant < half of glpK^m

g_interpretation.readout: acetate secretion rate (Cedex), exponential phase, biological duplicates
g_interpretation.outcome: overflow in CY02 and glpK^m-harboring mutants; ND in WT and crp^m (detection-limit bound, not absolute zero)

g_interpretation.readout: GABA titer in M9 + 0.2% glycerol + 50 mg/L yeast extract (HPLC-UV 215 nm, Primesep 100)

g_interpretation.intervention: switch to LB + 2% (v/v) glycerol; glycerol concentration screened by growth-rate proxy (Fig. S7, supplement unavailable)

g_interpretation.readout: 24 h time-course growth, glycerol, GABA in LB + 2% glycerol; biological triplicates

g_interpretation.intervention: lambda-Red deletion of ackA, mgsA, gabT singly and in combination
g_interpretation.readout: growth, glycerol, GABA in LB + 2% glycerol; biological triplicates
g_interpretation.outcome: CY02_TKO 0.59 ± 0.04 g/L and 0.13 ± 0.02 g/L/hr (Table 3); benefit absent in WT background

a_interpretation.name: Aldolase screen for HCHO+ACALD condensation (PDO production module)
a_interpretation.intervention: coexpression of candidate aldolases with DhaT in E. coli BL21(DE3)
a_interpretation.conditions: 10 mM HCHO + 10 mM ACALD, 2 h preliminary trial
outcomes: DERA_ECO 1.02 ± 0.03 mM PDO; other aldolases ≤0.038 mM

a_interpretation.name: 13C labeling verification of PDO carbon origin
a_interpretation.intervention: biosynthesis with 13C-HCHO or 13C-ACALD as cosubstrate
outcomes: peak ratios essentially identical between unlabeled standard and labeled samples; authors conclude PDO synthesis depends on added HCHO and ACALD

a_interpretation.name: Comparison of DERAs from different origins in vivo
objects: BF07-BF10-type strains coexpressing DERA variants with DhaT
a_interpretation.intervention: coexpression of DERA_TMA/ECO/GTH/SEP/PAE with DhaT
a_interpretation.conditions: 12 h bioconversion with HCHO and ACALD

a_interpretation.name: In vitro DERA activity and HCHO tolerance
objects: purified DERA_ECO, DERA_TMA, DERA_ECO C47M/C47V, DERA_Rd3BB, DERA_TMA C65M
a_interpretation.intervention: enzyme assay at 5-200 mM HCHO / 20 mM ACALD; 0.3 M HCHO 2 h pre-treatment vs 0 M control
outcomes: DERA_TMA 1.27 ± 0.02 U/mg at 10 mM HCHO; mutants retain 85-99% activity after 0.3 M HCHO vs 50-61% for wild types

a_interpretation.name: Km determination of DERA_TMA for HCHO
a_interpretation.intervention: activity measurements at 1-10 mM HCHO

a_interpretation.name: ACALD supply module: batch bioconversion ethanol + HCHO
a_interpretation.intervention: HpADH1 coexpression to oxidize ethanol to ACALD
a_interpretation.conditions: 5 mL, 50 mM Na2HPO4 pH 7.0, 300 mM ethanol, 100 mM HCHO, OD600 = 50, 30 °C, 230 rpm, capped 10 mL tubes
outcomes: 5.67 ± 0.25 mM (0.057 mol/mol) without HpADH1 vs 10.91 ± 0.08 mM (0.11 mol/mol) with HpADH1

a_interpretation.name: frmA knockout batch bioconversion
a_interpretation.intervention: CRISPR-Cas9 deletion of frmA
a_interpretation.conditions: as EXP6
readouts: PDO concentration and yield, HCHO consumption
outcomes: 12.75 ± 0.44 mM (0.97 ± 0.03 g/L), 0.128 mol/mol; reduced HCHO consumption

a_interpretation.name: Methanol-based HCHO supply module
a_interpretation.intervention: Mdh2 expression to oxidize methanol to HCHO
a_interpretation.conditions: whole-cell bioconversion with methanol and ethanol
outcomes: only 1.05 mM PDO after 42 h; Mdh activity is bottleneck (Figure S1E, unavailable)

a_interpretation.name: Diol byproduct identification and HCHO-dependence
a_interpretation.intervention: 13C-ethanol labeling; in vitro byproduct assay at varied HCHO/ACALD concentrations
outcomes: 1,3-BDO, C5 and C6 diol aldehydes identified; byproducts form only when HCHO nearly depleted; >0.6 mM HCHO strongly inhibits ACALD self-/cross-condensation in vitro

a_interpretation.name: Fed-batch bioconversion with interim HCHO addition
a_interpretation.intervention: fed-batch addition of 100 mM HCHO in ten interval additions to keep HCHO >0.6 mM
a_interpretation.conditions: 40 mL whole-cell system (Results) / 50 mL tube (Methods), initial 100 mM HCHO + 300 mM ethanol
readouts: PDO, methanol, formate, ACALD, 3-HPA over time
outcomes: 17.35 ± 0.58 mM (1.32 ± 0.04 g/L) PDO, 0.096 mol/mol at 24 h; no diol byproducts; methanol 56.47 mM at 30 h; some formate still formed

a_interpretation.name: Inverter_V1 construction and proof-of-concept characterization
a_interpretation.intervention: three-plasmid inverter assembly and transformation
a_interpretation.outcome: No significant RFP activation across tryptophan gradient (Figure 1e)

a_interpretation.name: Component troubleshooting of the two repression systems
a_interpretation.intervention: separate characterization of PtrpO1(G3C)-Plpp0.03-TrpR1(V58K) (tryptophan 0-125 mg/L) and PLlacO1-TetR/PtetO1-GFP tunability (IPTG 0-50 uM); then TetR degradation-tag variants
a_interpretation.outcome: TrpR1 system responded to 0-125 mg/L tryptophan; PtetO1-TetR showed extreme repression at low IPTG without dose dependence; TetR_LAA variant restored dose-dependent repression (0-50 uM IPTG)

a_interpretation.name: Characterization of degradation-tag inverter variants V1.1/V1.2
a_interpretation.intervention: tetR_DSA / tetR_LAA introduced into Inverter_V1

a_interpretation.name: RBS engineering to reduce TetR abundance
a_interpretation.intervention: random mutagenesis of RBS positions 6-9 of PtrpO1(G3C); screening of repression-system variants; selected RBS(G7T)/(A8G)/(G9C) built into inverters
a_interpretation.outcome: All RBS variants kept repression efficiency with lower leakiness (Figure S2); Inverter_V1.2.1 reached 2208+/-5.0 a.u., 5-fold over 440+/-21.1 a.u. baseline; V1.1.1 showed 7.38-fold dynamic range

a_interpretation.name: PtetO1 promoter and RBS engineering
a_interpretation.intervention: random mutations in -10 region of PtetO1 and its RBS; variants introduced into Inverter_V1.1.1/V1.2.1
a_interpretation.outcome: PtetO1-RBS(A2C) highest (2.21-fold over wildtype); V1.2.1e max 2316.3+/-75.5 a.u. (4.8-fold); V1.1.1e max 1485.1+/-48.5 a.u. (6.8-fold)

a_interpretation.name: Host engineering and simplified-configuration inverters (XG2/XG3)
a_interpretation.intervention: ubiC deletion; chromosomal Plpp0.03-TrpR(V58K)-T1 integration; two-plasmid inverter transfer
controls: XG1 with two-plasmid constitutive repression system (repression test)

a_interpretation.name: Bifunctional circuit characterization (population and single-cell)
a_interpretation.intervention: addition of PtrpO1(G3C)-GFP repression module to Inverter_V2.1.1/V2.2.1

conditions.imaging: 1% low-melting agarose immobilization, light-sheet microscopy, 50 ms exposure

a_interpretation.outcome: RFP up and GFP down with increasing tryptophan; no inter-module interference at single-cell level; Dual_V2.1.1 lower leaky expression than Dual_V2.2.1

a_interpretation.name: Tryptophan production monitoring in fermentation
a_interpretation.intervention: PLlacO1-trpE_fbrG addition and RFP_ASV reporter; IPTG induction
a_interpretation.outcome: RFP tracked tryptophan accumulation; full activation at 42 h; TRPdual_LAA bifunctionality from 30 h with GFP slightly increasing then repressed

a_interpretation.name: Dynamic up-regulation of tryptamine production
a_interpretation.intervention: CrTDC under low (PtetO1-RBS(A8G)) or high (PtetO1-RBS(A2C)) dynamic promoters in TRPactive_DSA

conditions.seed: 400 uL into 20 mL M9-2Y, 125 mL flask

controls: TM_Control (Plpp0.5-CrTDC; strength comparable to fully activated PtetO1-RBS(A2C), Figure S6a)
a_interpretation.outcome: TM_Low highest titer 36.9+/-2.8 mg/L at 48 h, 2.0-fold over TM_Control; experimental groups had residual tryptophan

a_interpretation.name: Dynamic up-regulation of violacein production
a_interpretation.intervention: vioAC and vioEBD operons under high/low dynamic promoter combinations in TRPactive_LAA

conditions.seed: 1 mL into 20 mL M9-2Y; 37 C 3.5 h then 0.5 mM IPTG; 30 C 48 h

a_interpretation.outcome: Vio_LH and Vio_HH exceeded control by 4.5-fold and 5.7-fold at 48 h; high-level dynamic vioAC up-regulation most beneficial

a_interpretation.name: Bifunctional regulation of violacein production
a_interpretation.intervention: PtrpO1(G3C)-plsB repression operon added to Vio_HH (Viodual_HH)
a_interpretation.outcome: Viodual_HH 10.5+/-0.6 mg/L; 7.4-fold over Vio_0.5 (1.4+/-0.1 mg/L) and 1.3-fold over Vio_HH-0.5 (8.0+/-0.4 mg/L)

a_interpretation.name: FC1 construction and growth test on CO2+FA
a_interpretation.intervention: Introduce reconstructed THF cycle, reverse glycine cleavage reaction and CbFdh into DH5α_GTPS
a_interpretation.conditions: M9 + 4.43 g/L sodium FA; 10% CO2/18% O2/72% N2; 37 °C; 200 r.p.m.; flask
controls: FC2/FC3/FC5 compared in same figure panel (Fig. 1b)
a_interpretation.outcome: FC1 failed to grow on CO2 and FA alone

a_interpretation.name: Stepwise construction of FC2, FC3, FC5 and growth tests
a_interpretation.intervention: ppsA overexpression + ppsR deletion (FC2); purT deletion (FC3); p100FA2 harbouring A. thaliana fdh_mut (FC5)
a_interpretation.conditions: as EXP-01
controls: growth with 0.1 g/L glucose supplementation every 24 h (Extended Data Fig. 1b)
a_interpretation.outcome: FC5 grew on CO2+FA alone to OD600 0.285 (0.0633 g DCW/L) in 150 h from OD600 0.051; ~2.5 doublings; c.f.u. increased

a_interpretation.name: 13C isotope analysis of FC1 and FC2
a_interpretation.conditions: M9 + 0.1 g/L [U-13C]glucose + 4.43 g/L sodium FA; 100-ml baffled flask/30 ml; 37 °C; 200 r.p.m.; 10% CO2 atmosphere; sampling at 120 h
readouts: 12C/13C ratios in proteinogenic amino acids by GC-MS
a_interpretation.outcome: Isotope ratios of Ala, Phe, Tyr, Val, Thr, Asp, Glu, Gly, Ser compared between FC1 and FC2 (Extended Data Fig. 2)

a_interpretation.name: FC5 substrate-dependency test
a_interpretation.conditions: CO2+FA, FA only, CO2 only, without CO2 and FA
a_interpretation.outcome: Growth characterized under each supplementation condition (Extended Data Fig. 3)

a_interpretation.name: 13C confirmation of CO2/FA assimilation by FC5
a_interpretation.conditions: 13C-labelled preculture then CO2+FA only; sampling at 100 h
readouts: increase of 12C ratios in proteinogenic amino acids
a_interpretation.outcome: CO2 and FA assimilation confirmed (Extended Data Fig. 4)

a_interpretation.name: IPTG concentration and aeration optimization of FC5
a_interpretation.intervention: Vary IPTG (1, 0.1, 0.05 mM) and aeration (flask type/working volume)
a_interpretation.conditions: as EXP-01 with varied inducer/aeration
controls: mRNA ratios normalized to 1 mM IPTG condition
a_interpretation.outcome: Optimized conditions gave OD600 0.533 in 200 h from OD600 0.07; selected IPTG concentration not stated in available text

a_interpretation.name: Plasmid copy-number tuning (FC7, FC8)
a_interpretation.intervention: Replace high-copy plasmid system of FC5 with medium- (FC7) or low-copy (FC8) plasmids
a_interpretation.conditions: as EXP-01
controls: FC5 growth profile as comparator (Fig. 1d dashed line)
a_interpretation.outcome: FC8 OD600 0.607 in 200 h (0.14-fold above FC5); FC7 OD600 0.452; FC8 showed higher CO2/FA assimilation and FA consumption than FC5

a_interpretation.name: FC8 high-inoculum flask culture (OD600 0.35)
a_interpretation.conditions: initial OD600 0.35; 37 °C; flask; CO2+FA
a_interpretation.outcome: OD600 1.24 (0.343 g DCW/L) in 100 h; cell filamentation observed

a_interpretation.name: Cultivation temperature optimization of FC8
a_interpretation.intervention: Reduce cultivation temperature (30, 32, 33 °C tested; 37 °C reference)
a_interpretation.conditions: CO2+FA flask cultivation at reduced temperatures
a_interpretation.outcome: 32 °C best: OD600 2.48 (0.687 g DCW/L) in 244 h from OD600 0.31, 0.41 g FA consumed; biomass yield 0.0552±0.0009 vs 0.0365±0.0026 g DCW/g FA (32 vs 37 °C); cyoAB up / cydAB down as intended; filamentation suppressed

a_interpretation.name: FC8 low-inoculum flask culture (OD600 0.018)
a_interpretation.conditions: initial OD600 0.018; flask; CO2+FA
a_interpretation.outcome: OD600 3.59 (0.994 g DCW/L) in 791.5 h; 0.94 g FA consumed; 7.64 doublings; growth rate declined over time

a_interpretation.name: FC8 bioreactor fed-batch cultivations
a_interpretation.intervention: Fed-batch bioreactor cultivation with pH-stat FA feeding
a_interpretation.conditions: 1.3-l Bioflow 110, 500 ml working volume; 32 °C; 500 r.p.m. initial (second run ramped +50 r.p.m. per OD600 up to 750); pH 6.8 via 30 v/v% FA; air:CO2 9:1 at 500 ml/min; initial OD600 ~1
a_interpretation.outcome: Max OD600 7.38 (450 h), 7.88 (412 h), 8.01 (412 h), 11.1 (577 h) across four runs; summarized as OD600 7-11

a_interpretation.purpose: Design and construct high-resolution genome-scale CRISPRi sgRNA library
a_interpretation.intervention: In silico sgRNA design (23-mers at NGG PAMs, 100-nt CDS windows, BLASTN off-target filtering, fixed 'A' upstream of spacer); oligo pool synthesis (CustomArray); extension PCR; Gibson/NEBuilder HiFi assembly into pgRNA backbone (40 ng insert : 100 ng backbone, 40 µL); electroporation into Endura; plating on 87 LB-agar+ampicillin plates
a_interpretation.conditions: LB agar 25 cm × 25 cm, ampicillin 100 µg/mL; pooled colonies cultured in liquid LB to OD 1.0
a_interpretation.readouts: Amplicon sequencing of plasmid pool (HiSeq 2500, SE 150 bp); library composition QC
a_interpretation.analysis: sgRNA representation counting vs designed pool
a_interpretation.tested_scope: E. coli MG1655 CDS (RefSeq NC_000913.3); LB condition for library amplification

a_interpretation.purpose: Genome-wide gene fitness under gentamicin and anaerobic conditions
a_interpretation.intervention: Electroporation of 100 ng library plasmids into MG1655+pdCas9; pooled growth under three conditions with dCas9-mediated knockdown

conditions.anaerobic_LB: N2 headspace 100 kPa, 37°C, 9 h, to OD600 0.6

controls: initial plasmid library without dCas9 co-expression (ER baseline)
a_interpretation.readouts: sgRNA abundance by amplicon NGS (HiSeq 2500, SE 150 bp)
a_interpretation.analysis: ER per gene = median of normalized sgRNA ratios; Pearson correlation; PCA; COG categorization (>1.5-fold ER change)
a_interpretation.outcomes: Gene-level fitness maps for LB, gentamicin, anaerobic; gentamicin vs anaerobic ER correlation r = 0.93; condition-specific ER changes for ribosomal, TA, OMP, efflux, cofactor-biosynthesis genes
a_interpretation.tested_scope: E. coli MG1655, LB, gentamicin 1 µg/mL, anaerobiosis as defined

a_interpretation.purpose: Transcriptomic changes under gentamicin and anaerobic conditions; iModulon activities of ArcA/CpxR regulons
a_interpretation.intervention: Culture in LB, LB + 1 µg/mL gentamicin, anaerobic LB (same protocol as screen); RNAsnap RNA extraction; Ribo-Zero rRNA depletion; TruSeq Stranded mRNA library
a_interpretation.conditions: as EXP2; triplicate
controls: P1K public transcriptome compendium as iModulon reference (external data, background_citation)
a_interpretation.analysis: CLC mapping (0.9/0.9); DESeq2; DEG >2.0-fold, Padj<0.001; iModulon projection (pymodulon, P1K)
a_interpretation.outcomes: 2,348 gentamicin-induced DEGs; specific regulation of ArcA and CpxR iModulons; CpxR iModulon activity under gentamicin exceeding ethanol-stress reference; ArcA activity suppressed under gentamicin

a_interpretation.purpose: Validate screen-implicated genes by growth of single-gene knockouts under gentamicin
a_interpretation.intervention: Growth profiling of KEIO deletion strains vs wild type under gentamicin 1 µg/mL (strains constructed by ref 58, used here)
a_interpretation.conditions: LB + gentamicin 1 µg/mL; microplate monitoring

replicates.scope: FIG 4C cofactor-gene panel; replicate count for FIG 5B not separately stated

a_interpretation.analysis: SD error bars; Welch's t-test, P < 0.1
a_interpretation.outcomes: Δfre, ΔubiX, ΔubiC, ΔhemX less sensitive; ΔbhsA completely resistant; ΔarcA/ΔarcB/ΔcpxR more sensitive; ΔcpxA little effect
a_interpretation.tested_scope: listed nine deletions, gentamicin 1 µg/mL, LB
unsupported_extensions: exact growth-rate values and per-strain statistics (figure visual and source data unavailable)

a_interpretation.purpose: Genome-wide CpxR binding under LB, anaerobic, and gentamicin conditions
a_interpretation.intervention: Chromosomal c-myc C-terminal tagging of cpxR (method of ref 65); ChIP with anti-c-Myc 9E10; sequencing
a_interpretation.conditions: 25 mL cultures; 1% formaldehyde crosslinking 30 min RT; sonication 10×20 s; IP overnight 4°C

replicates.n: >=2 (peaks in two or more replicates counted as binding events)

a_interpretation.analysis: CLC mapping; MACS2 default; DOOR2.0 operons
a_interpretation.outcomes: 933 binding positions under gentamicin vs 51 (anaerobic) and 13 (LB); CpxR regulon estimated at 1,611 genes; binding at nuo/cyo/cyd regulatory regions and arcA

a_interpretation.purpose: Test CpxR dependence of membrane-potential collapse under gentamicin
a_interpretation.intervention: DiOC2 staining after exposure to aerobic LB, anaerobic LB, CCCP 5 µM, or gentamicin 1 µg/mL
a_interpretation.conditions: cultures to OD600 1.0 (aerobic) / 0.6 (anaerobic); 1×10^6 cells/mL in filtered PBS; 30 min staining
